AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

messages.content:
I acquired the tapping-mode image and processed it; the RMS roughness after levelling is **0.31 nm**.

- **Acquisition:** The scan ran in PhaseContrast mode with the requested settings. The instrument read back 5 µm × 5 µm, 512 × 512 pixels, 0.075 s per line, P/I/D 100/50/10 and setpoint 70%. The file contains amplitude and phase channels, which fits tapping mode. Its name starts with "lfm_", which normally means lateral force mode; I didn't look into that.
- **Processing:** I fitted and subtracted a straight line from each scan line, then subtracted a fitted plane. Both the line-only and line-plus-plane versions gave 0.307 nm on the forward Z-Axis height channel.
- **Why levelling was needed:** The unprocessed RMS is 1155.26 nm. That figure mostly reflects a large height drift, not surface roughness. Average row height falls from about 4.7 µm in the first rows to about −1.5 µm by roughly row 64, then stays near −1.45 µm.
- **Caveat:** The drift at the start looks like the tip settling at the beginning of the frame. Those rows are still included in the 0.31 nm figure, though line levelling removes their offsets.

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

The scan is done and the feedback engaged correctly. After the first 80 lines, the amplitude settled at about 0.34 V, roughly 68% of the 0.498 V seen at the start. That matches the 70% setpoint.

Other results for reference:

- **Whole frame, line-levelled:** Ra = 0.25 nm.

I acquired one phase-contrast image with the requested settings. After line-levelling, the mean roughness (Ra) is **0.27 nm**.

- **Acquisition:** the scan used 5 µm × 5 µm, 512 × 512 pixels, 0.075 s per line, P/I/D 100/50/10 and a 70% amplitude setpoint. The instrument read all of these values back as set.
- **Settling transient:** the raw height data falls from about +4.7 µm to −1.5 µm over roughly the first 64 lines, then stays steady. Unprocessed, this gives Ra ≈ 640.7 nm, which reflects the drift rather than the surface.
- **Processing:** I removed a straight-line fit from each scan line, then computed Ra over the whole image.

messages.content:
I acquired the lateral-force image and the average friction is 0.000305 V, but about the first 48 of 256 lines are a settling transient that this average includes.

**Settings applied:** Lateral Force mode, 5 µm × 5 µm, 256 × 256 pixels, 0.075 s per line, setpoint 0.1 V, P/I/D 100/50/0. The instrument read back all of these as set.

**Friction result:** Friction here is half of forward minus backward on the lateral channel, signed and averaged over every pixel. That gives 0.000305 V (about 0.3 mV); the RMS friction is 0.000498 V.

**Settling transient:** Over roughly the first 48 lines, Z height falls steadily from about +4.5 µm to about −1.7 µm. After that it stays near −1.67 µm, with about 4 nm of variation along each line. This looks like the feedback settling into contact rather than Z being pinned at its limit. The raw lateral signal also drifts over the frame (about 8 mV in the first rows, about 3 mV in the last). I did not recompute the average using only the settled lines, and I did not rescan.

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.
